title: 2_Sum and Product of Roots

findings.finding: The p5 examples use polynomial substitution and linear equations with fractional constants without prerequisite rehearsal.
findings.breakdown: Students must recall substitution structure and isolate an unknown while learning how root relationships determine roots and coefficients.
findings.checked: Searched all preceding teaching. The p3 derivation and p4 factorisation and root-expression tasks do not rehearse polynomial evaluation or solving these equations. Both skills are substantial steps in the p5 worked examples, rather than final simplifications.
findings.assumptions: These are prior algebra skills. A calculator does not supply substitution structure or equation rearrangement.

repair.proposal: Immediately before p5-paired-example-block, add four short review items: (a) For P(x)=2x²−7x+3, calculate P(3). Answer: 0. (b) Solve 2+t=7/2. Answer: t=3/2. (c) Solve 3u=−2. Answer: u=−2/3. (d) Solve −5v=8/9. Answer: v=−8/45. Keep this rehearsal within one page.

findings.doneWhen: Students rehearse substitution and linear equation solving immediately before the p5 applications.

findings.finding: Extend the root-shift question to compare the original and shifted root differences.
findings.breakdown: The follow-up connects changing sums and products with an unchanged difference.
findings.checked: The original roots have sum 3 and product 10. Adding 4 gives sum 11 and product 38; the squared difference is 9−40=−31 before and after shifting. No explicit complex-root calculations are required.
findings.assumptions: Uses the same interpretation of roots already required by p10-q15; the separate context question concerns that existing interpretation.

repair.proposal: After the existing task add: (b) Find the quadratic equation with roots α+4 and β+4. Answer: x²−11x+38=0. (c) Find (α−β)². Answer: −31. (d) Find [(α+4)−(β+4)]². Answer: −31. (e) Explain why adding 4 to both roots leaves their difference unchanged. Answer: the added 4s cancel on subtraction.

findings.doneWhen: The follow-up uses the existing roots and compares their differences before and after shifting.

findings.finding: Extend the existing shifted product with consecutive shifts to expose the different weights on the symmetric root sums.
findings.breakdown: For shift t, the product is 3/2−t/2−5t²/2+t³; a shift of one conceals the different powers of t.
findings.checked: Checked the expansion and all proposed values. Existing part a already asks for αβγ, so the proposed duplicate shift-zero part is unnecessary. Existing part e followed by shifts 2, 3 and 4 supplies four consecutive comparison questions.
findings.assumptions: Expansion and grouping into symmetric sums are available from p12-example-b.

repair.proposal: Immediately before existing part e add: “Predict how changing the number added to each root changes the expansion.” After e, under the existing instruction, add (f) (α+2)(β+2)(γ+2), answer −3/2; (g) (α+3)(β+3)(γ+3), answer 9/2; (h) (α+4)(β+4)(γ+4), answer 47/2. Follow with unpatterned part (i) (α−1)(β−1)(γ−1), answer −3/2. The polynomial stays fixed while the common shift varies.

findings.doneWhen: The shift-one task and three added shifts form a consecutive run followed by an unpatterned task.

findings.finding: p29-q10 repeats the complete task in p28-q6 with only coefficient letters changed.
findings.breakdown: Both tasks require the same opposite-root and reciprocal-root representation and prove the same two coefficient relationships.
findings.checked: Compared both complete stems, givens and conclusions. The correspondence p,q,r,s ↔ a,b,c,d leaves the whole mathematical task unchanged. Neither task states a retrieval or comparison purpose. For the replacement, roots t,−t,u,v with uv=2 give b=2−t², d=−2t² and c=−at², hence b=2+d/2 and c=ad/2.
findings.assumptions: Renaming symbolic coefficients does not create a distinct practice task.

repair.proposal: Replace p29-q10-root with: “The polynomial P(x)=x⁴+ax³+bx²+cx+d has two zeroes that are opposites and two other zeroes whose product is 2. Show that b=2+d/2 and c=ad/2.” Answers: b=2+d/2 and c=ad/2.

findings.doneWhen: The later copy retains its proof structure but uses product 2 and the corresponding different conclusions.

findings.finding: Add a consecutive run changing only the leading coefficient to expose its effect on all four symmetric root sums.
findings.breakdown: Keeping the other coefficients fixed makes their division by the leading coefficient visible.
findings.checked: Checked every answer against p26-theory. The existing three parts do not provide this comparison. Placing the new parts immediately after existing part a makes the proposed run consecutive.
findings.assumptions: Uses only the quartic formulas supplied immediately before practice.

repair.proposal: Immediately after existing part a, add: “Predict how each answer changes as the leading coefficient changes.” Under the existing instruction insert three parts: 2x⁴+2x³−x²−x+5=0; 3x⁴+2x³−x²−x+5=0; 4x⁴+2x³−x²−x+5=0. Answers in sum, pair-sum, triple-sum, product order are respectively (−1,−1/2,1/2,5/2), (−2/3,−1/3,1/3,5/3), and (−1/2,−1/4,1/4,5/4). Follow this run with 3x⁴−6x³+9x²+12x−15=0, answers (2,3,−4,−5). Retain the original b and c after these additions and relabel consecutively.

findings.doneWhen: Four consecutive tasks vary only the leading coefficient and are followed by an unpatterned task.

findings.finding: The geometry topic combines root testing, midpoint calculation, gradient and Pythagoras without an opening review of those prior methods.
findings.breakdown: The guided examples require students to recall several coordinate and polynomial procedures while connecting polynomial roots to intersections and distances.
findings.checked: Searched all supplied teaching and the preceding quartic practice. No opening review rehearses these methods. The quadratic topic models substitution, but not immediately before this topic. The p31 identity teaches horizontal separation, so it is excluded from the missing review pieces. Midpoint calculation and the gradient-to-Pythagoras route remain substantial prior steps.
findings.assumptions: These are prior skills, consistent with the separate Polynomials and Coordinate Geometry booklets. Calculator use does not change the recall demands.

repair.proposal: Before p30-theory add: (a) For P(x)=x³−4x²+x+6, calculate P(−1) and P(2), and state the corresponding factors. Answers: both 0; x+1 and x−2. (b) Find the midpoint of A(−2,−6) and B(4,6). Answer: (1,0). (c) Two points on y=2x−2 have horizontal separation 3. Find their vertical separation. Answer: 6. (d) Hence find their exact distance apart. Answer: 3√5. Keep the review within one page.

findings.doneWhen: The opening review rehearses root testing, midpoint calculation and the gradient-to-Pythagoras distance route.

findings.finding: Follow the non-origin tangent with the tangent whose point of contact is the origin.
findings.breakdown: The follow-up compares two locations of the repeated intersection root using the same root-sum methods.
findings.checked: With roots 0,0,r, the sum gives r=5 and the pair-sum gives 6−m=0. For m=6, the intersection polynomial is x²(x−5), confirming double contact at the origin.
findings.assumptions: Uses the interpretation of double roots taught in p30-theory and the coefficient relationships already used in p34-q5-c.

repair.proposal: After p34-q5-d add: (e) Now suppose y=mx is tangent to the cubic at the origin, so the intersection roots are 0,0,r. Find r using the sum of roots. Answer: r=5. (f) Use the sum of products taken two at a time to find m. Answer: 6−m=0, so m=6. (g) State this tangent’s equation. Answer: y=6x.

findings.doneWhen: The added parts use the existing cubic to find its tangent at the origin.

contextQuestions.question: Have students already learned to interpret non-real roots, or are formal calculations with them intended to be introduced here? The first Your Turn uses 2x²+3x+5=0 and gives a negative sum of squares, while the supplied teaching does not explain that interpretation before p10-q17.

protectedGroups.observation: Multiplying every coefficient by the same nonzero factor leaves the roots, their sum and their product unchanged.
protectedGroups.invariant: The quadratic factor after removing the common factor, its roots, and the coefficient ratios.

protectedGroups.observation: An expansion becomes an identity that evaluates a root expression without finding the individual roots.
protectedGroups.invariant: The relationship between the square of the sum, the sum of squares and twice the product.

importReview: Lean content review table: 83 of 83 blocks passed.
